08 — Oscillators

Commodity Channel Index#

Heuristic1 min read
◆ The PatternHow far price has strayed from its typical level, measured in units of its usual wandering

// How far price has strayed from its typical level, measured in units of its usual wandering

The Commodity Channel Index — created by Donald Lambert (1980).

CCI = (Typical Price − SMA(TP)) / (0.015 × Mean Deviation)

The 0.015 constant scales the indicator so that roughly 70–80% of values fall between −100 and +100 (Lambert’s intent).

Interpretation:
• CCI > +100 → unusually strong (possible overbought)
• CCI < −100 → unusually weak (possible oversold)
• Zero-line crossovers indicate trend direction changes
Worked example

Day 15: the typical prices of days 11–15 are 103.67, 102.33, 99.67, 100.67 and 103.33. Their mean is 101.93 and their mean absolute deviation 1.41, so CCI = (103.33 − 101.93) / (0.015 × 1.41) = 66. Two days earlier, at the low, it read −141, below Lambert’s −100 line. The 0.015 was chosen so that most readings land between −100 and +100.

Where it misleads
  • It has no bound: readings of ±200 or ±300 happen in strong moves, and fading them means fading a trend.
  • The mean deviation shrinks in quiet periods, so a modest move after a calm stretch gives an extreme reading.
  • Lambert built it to catch cycles in commodities; where there is no regular cycle the ±100 lines have no special meaning.
In code
tp = (df['high'] + df['low'] + df['close']) / 3
ma = tp.rolling(5).mean()
md = tp.rolling(5).apply(lambda x: np.abs(x - x.mean()).mean(), raw=True)
df['cci5'] = (tp - ma) / (0.015 * md)

Assumes import numpy as np, import pandas as pd, and a DataFrame df with columns high, low, close and volume — the 15 days above.

Sources
  • D. R. Lambert, “Commodity Channel Index: Tools for Trading Cyclic Trends”, Commodities magazine, 1980
  • Technical Analysis from A to Z (2nd ed.), S. B. Achelis, McGraw-Hill, 2000
  • C.-H. Park & S. H. Irwin, “What Do We Know About the Profitability of Technical Analysis?”, Journal of Economic Surveys 21(4), 2007 — a review of the evidence across studies
Pattern bridge: CCI measures deviation from the mean in units of mean absolute deviation — a z-score variant. In ML, batch normalization does the same: center and scale.
